issues.legal_issue: A state legislature may exclude specified expenditure from deductions when computing agricultural income, including expenditure on immature plants that produce no income in the relevant year.
material_facts: The company incurred expenditure on the upkeep and maintenance of immature rubber plants from which no agricultural income was derived in the relevant year.
The Court had previously held that the expenditure was deductible under the existing agricultural income-tax law.
The legislature subsequently amended the law to disallow that expenditure.
issues.conclusion: The legislature was competent to enact the amendment disallowing the deduction, and the amendment was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Article 366(1) ties the meaning of agricultural income to its definition for Indian income-tax purposes, while Entry 46 of List II empowers a state legislature to tax agricultural income. The word “income” has a wide ordinary meaning and is not necessarily limited to receipts net of all necessary expenses. A legislature may determine which deductions are permitted when computing taxable agricultural income. The Court relied on Navinchandra Mafatlal v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay and distinguished the prior decision in Travancore Rubber & Tea Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Agricultural Income-tax, Kerala, which had interpreted the earlier deduction provision.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_agricultural_income_tax_law and state_legislates_on_agricultural_income and expenditure_is_for_immature_plants and plants_produce_no_income_in_relevant_year

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_agricultural: A party challenges the validity of a state law that taxes agricultural income.
predicates.state_legislates_on_agricultural_income: The state legislature makes rules for taxing agricultural income and determining deductions in its computation.
predicates.expenditure_is_for_immature_plants: The taxpayer incurs expenditure to cultivate, upkeep, or maintain immature plants.
predicates.plants_produce_no_income_in_relevant_yea: The immature plants produce no agricultural income for the year used to compute the taxpayer’s income.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns a state law taxing agricultural income, and the disputed expenditure maintains immature plants that produce no income in the relevant year, the legislature may validly exclude that expenditure from deductions.

issues.legal_issue: A deduction rule that treats agricultural income from rubber plantations differently from income from tea plantations is not discriminatory when the two kinds of income are subject to materially different computation arrangements.
material_facts: The amendment disallowed expenditure on immature plants from the computation of agricultural income from crops other than tea.
Income from the sale of tea grown and manufactured by the seller was partly agricultural and partly business income.
Special rules provided for separating the agricultural and business portions of tea income.
Income from the sale of rubber was not divided between agricultural and business income in the same way.
issues.conclusion: The different treatment of rubber and tea income was based on relevant differences and did not contravene Article 14.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not prohibit different treatment grounded in relevant differences between the classes being compared. The Court relied on Karimtharuvi Tea Estates Ltd. v. State of Kerala, which had determined that the amendment did not apply to agricultural income from tea plantations because of the special rules for computing the agricultural portion of tea income under the Indian Income-tax Act and rules made under it.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_crop_based_t: A party challenges the constitutionality of a tax rule that treats income from different crops differently.
predicates.deduction_rule_treats_crops_differently: The disputed deduction rule applies differently to income associated with different crops.
predicates.one_crop_income_has_separate_agricultura: Income from one crop includes both an agricultural component and a business component.
predicates.other_crop_income_does_not_have_the_same: Income from the other crop is not divided into those same agricultural and business components.
predicates.special_computation_rules_apply_to_the_m: Special rules govern how the agricultural and business components of the mixed income are computed.

issues.definition: Different treatment is not discriminatory when a challenged crop-based tax rule distinguishes crops whose income has different components and special computation rules apply to the mixed income.
